record.excerpt: The market makes a new 20day high or low and the previous high/low marker must have been at least 3 trading sessions prior. … The close of the new high/low must be greater than (beyond) the previous high/low price marker. … Buy entry is placed on the next day at the previous 20 day high/low watermark … Stop entries for failed trades are placed below the latest high/low that triggered the signal … Profits/exits should be taken within 2-6 candlestick intervals … OHLCV historical data for Bitcoin (BTC) from Binance exchange.
record.notes: Turtle Soup 20-day false-breakout rule on Binance BTC daily; exit window 2-6 bars is a range (compiler must pick).

spec.claim_summary: Bitcoin buys a new 20-day high close beyond a marker at least 3 sessions old and exits within 2-6 bars with a stop below the trigger extreme.
assumptions: Timeframe 1d assumed as most natural reading for 20day highs and candlestick intervals; claim states no bar length.
Entry uses close above previous 20-bar highest_high to represent a new 20-day high close beyond the previous marker; next-bar open fill approximates next-day entry.
Three-session age filter compiled as 3-bar highest_high below 20-bar highest_high, so the 20-day marker comes from more than 3 sessions prior.
NOT EXPRESSIBLE: new 20-day low trigger for a Buy cannot be expressed because entry conditions combine with AND only; this spec tests the high-breakout side and omits the low-breakout Buy side.
NOT EXPRESSIBLE: next-day entry at the previous 20 day high/low watermark price cannot be expressed; the engine fills at the next bar open.
NOT EXPRESSIBLE: stop below the latest high/low that triggered the signal is an entry-anchored price-level stop and cannot be expressed as stop_loss_pct; no stop set.
Time exit within 2-6 intervals compiled as fixed max_hold_bars 4, the midpoint of the stated range.

issues.problem: Claim requires Buy on new 20-day high OR new 20-day low. Spec tests only the high-breakout side (close > 20-bar highest_high) and omits the low-breakout Buy side. Leaving out half the signals changes what is tested.
Claim requires stop below the latest high/low that triggered the signal. Spec sets no stop (null). Omitting the stop changes losses and verdict.
Claim requires next-day entry at the previous 20-day high/low watermark price. Spec fills at next bar open, a different price than the watermark limit level, which changes trade prices.

report.headline: Tested an approximation of the claim. Makes money (+0.76% per trade after costs, 71 trades) but can't be told from luck: random timing did as well 30% of the time.
reasons: makes money after costs (+0.76% per trade), but random timing did as well 30% of the time (p = 0.303); needs p < 0.05 to count as an edge
warnings: just holding did better: +44% vs buy-and-hold +1781%
